subject: Invites: Redwood multi-prospect webinar — regional block proposal
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Alice Moreno <alice@finova.com>, Carlos Mendes <carlos@acme-inc.com>, Priya Shah <priya@datasynth.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-14T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Invites: Redwood multi-prospect webinar — regional block proposal

Hi all,

Thanks for the quick interest in a group walkthrough of Redwood Inference. We’re putting together a 60-minute demo + short live Q&A tailored to teams evaluating inference economics and deployment options.

High-level plan:
- 20 min product walkthrough (runtime, cost controls, Dedicated/Private options)
- 20 min short technical deep-dive (KV cache, batching, SLO tuning)
- 20 min live Q&A + optional breakout rooms for 1:1 follow-ups

We wanted to run this as a single multi-prospect session on Tuesday, Aug 29. Proposed time: 10:00 AM PT / 1:00 PM ET / 6:00 PM BST (60 min).

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood-webinar-brief.pdf (PDF, 1.8MB)] and a tentative attendee list [Attachment: proposed-attendee-list.csv (CSV, 4 KB)].

Question for you — are there timezone conflicts that would make a single global slot difficult? If so we can split into two regional blocks (EMEA + APAC) with the same agenda.

Internal note: looping in Soojin and Ben to propose presenters and handle breakout rooms.

Next steps: please reply with your preference (single global slot vs regional split) and any agenda items you want covered.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
https://redwood.ai
From: Alice Moreno <alice@finova.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-14T19:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Invites: Redwood multi-prospect webinar — regional block proposal

Thanks Karthik — this looks great.

Quick note: our engineering and infra leads are in APAC (SG/Tokyo) and 10:00 AM PT would be late evening for them (early morning next day). They'd prefer an APAC-friendly block. A 9:00 AM SGT / 6:00 PM BST option would work best if you split.

If you do a single session we might only send product folks. Splitting would get us the infra folks involved.

— Alice
Director of Platform — Finova
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-15T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Invites: Redwood multi-prospect webinar — regional block proposal

Karthik — good catch from Alice. I recommend we do two regional blocks:

Option A — AM EMEA/US overlap (suits EMEA + East Coast): 08:00 PT / 11:00 ET / 16:00 BST — 60 min
Option B — APAC-friendly (late evening PT): 18:00 PT / 21:00 ET / 09:00 SGT (next day) — 60 min local for APAC

Ben, can you lead the APAC block (you presented last month and handled breakout rooms really well)? I’ll handle the technical deep-dive for EMEA/US.

Also suggest we prepare a one-page tailored slide for infra/ops for APAC attendees (KV cache + private deployment notes). I can draft that and add to the deck.

Soojin
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-08-15T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Invites: Redwood multi-prospect webinar — regional block proposal

Thanks Alice — appreciate the context.

We’ll split into two blocks and keep the same agenda. Please pick whichever slot works for your team:

1) EMEA / US-friendly: Tue Aug 29 — 11:00 AM ET / 4:00 PM BST (60 min)
2) APAC-friendly: Wed Aug 30 — 09:00 AM SGT / Tue 8:00 PM PT (60 min local)

We’ll run the same deck and open a breakout room per company for 15 min after the main session.

Calendar placeholders: 
- EMEA/US: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=emea_placeholder
- APAC: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=apac_placeholder

Attachments: updated brief + attendee list (see attached). If you can confirm which slot you prefer, we’ll send a calendar invite to lock it.

Internal: Marissa — can you drop the updated attendee CSV into the shared Drive and add a column for timezone? Ben — will follow-up on APAC breakout logistics.

Thanks,
Karthik
